upstream: FFmpeg n7.1.5; Firefox upstream FIREFOX_153_7_0esr_RELEASE 9aecd40e03ebf6e866e32a0a3001488ed751228d (Debian patch equivalence not asserted)

motivation.queue20_conclusion: Increasing the software video queue preference to20 did not resolve presentation drops. Earlier conditional preroll suggestion was tested and is not a demonstrated fix.
motivation.interpretation: Sink lateness is measured; GPU compositor is not the dominant drop source. The software decode control presents near60 fps. A v6 per-DecodePromise output batch size has not yet been measured on hardware.

design.firefox: FFmpegDataDecoder::ProcessDecode resolves results only after DoDecode returns; DoDecode receives repeatedly until EAGAIN, retaining earlier frames during later synchronous output copies.
design.target: Prioritize input consumption after the first output and publish at the next contract-safe EAGAIN point.
gate: Private H264/HEVC BSF has returned EAGAIN.
ff_decode_get_packet has returned EAGAIN, after consuming the generic FFmpeg input filterchain and buffer_pkt.
exceptions: Owned pending-AU backpressure retains bounded waits and may pull additional frames beyond the normal one-frame batch.
Replay64/pending65 first-frame wait retains its existing deadline and pending packet ownership.
EOS is not bounded by the output quota; all remaining frames drain before EOF.
design.reset: Flush clears batch counters; each contract-safe EAGAIN starts a fresh batch.
design.diagnostics: At most12 nonempty batch logs per generation. elapsed_us covers callback span and may include time between caller invocations; it is not a pure-copy measurement.

validation.runner: Actual ARM64 candidate shared libraries via qemu-aarch64-static and exported software stub, no sockets/devices
regression_cases: 64 startup packets and pending65 remain ordered; first output publishes then all65 EOS frames delivered
Real5s startup timeout falls back with all70 frames exact MD5/PTS/duration

validation.independent_summary: Actual v6/v7 ARM64 delay-stub A/B; final4009 v7 checks and4373 v6 checks including occupied FFmpeg input-slot EOS/flush.8ready frames with10ms copies: old batch8 adds72-74ms first-frame holding time; new normal batch1 under0.3ms.

limits: Host tests do not establish real-board improvement.
The normal one-frame target is not an absolute batch limit under broker backpressure or EOS.
Ready backend frames may remain until subsequent input or EOS; this is not a zero-buffering promise for every caller policy.
Do not interpret totalVideoFrames or rVFC presentedFrames as actual compositor throughput.
